standard_prerequisites: natural deduction derivations and their undischarged assumptions
finiteness of derivations as finite trees
consistency defined by absence of a derivation of a contradiction
core_obligations: Prove compactness for the natural-deduction calculus: (1) if Gamma proves A then a finite subset Gamma_0 of Gamma proves A; (2) if every finite subset of Gamma is consistent then Gamma is consistent
proof_roadmap: A derivation of A from Gamma is a finite derivation tree; take Gamma_0 to be its undischarged assumptions, a finite subset of Gamma; the same derivation witnesses Gamma_0 proves A
If Gamma is inconsistent there is a derivation of a contradiction from Gamma; its undischarged assumptions form a finite inconsistent subset
Clause (2) is the contrapositive of clause (1) for A = absurdity
difficulty_reason: Both clauses follow from finiteness of derivation trees via the undischarged-assumption reading; short but requires the correct reading of the derivability relation.
